newsitem.title: USA: Future Mars samples should be isolated - report.
newsitem.headline: Future Mars samples should be isolated - report.

text.p: Future Martian samples should be isolated when they are brought back to Earth to be on the safe side even though such samples pose little risk of contamination, a U.S. advisory panel recommended on Thursday.

"Because there are plausible scenarios in which samples taken from Mars could contain either active or dormant organisms, these samples should be isolated physically and biologically and regarded as hazardous until proved otherwise," the panel of experts said in a statement.

It said it was unlikely life as Earthlings know it exists on the surface of Mars, and if it does exist it is unlikely to be able to adapt to Earth or do significant harm here. But to be safe, they recommend isolating Martian samples on the trip back to Earth and say materials that come into contact with these samples should be sterilised or not brought to Earth.

Once on Earth, the isolated samples should be processed at a special receiving facility, which should be in operation at least two years before the launch of a sample-collecting mission to Mars, the panel said. This would allow time to develop the needed technologies for detection of life and for containment and sterilisation.

The study was funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, which announced in August that it may have found fossilized traces of microscopic life on a meteorite that perhaps originated on Mars and fell to Earth.

One way to confirm that the meteorite came from Mars would be to bring back similar samples of Martian rock with the same kinds of fossils. NASA chief Dan Goldin has said the earliest such samples might be recovered would be in 2003.
The National Research Council is a private, non-profit institution that provides advice on science and technology.
